answer: Divergent checkpoint attestation. Each identity keeps a private rolling transcript and, at network-chosen checkpoints, signs a Merkle root plus a response to a fresh challenge. Any two identities whose checkpoint/challenge pair collides are rejected. Clones share state, so they emit the same ripple of signed hashes and cannot pass as separate agents. Peers hold a mirror copy of prior checkpoints and compare. Each identity also commits a branching interaction orchard, forcing unique history.
